headline: Bodies of 5 Bangladeshis killed in Qatar road crash arrive home
summary: The remains of five expatriate workers who died in a tragic road accident in Qatar were flown back to Bangladesh.
details: The bodies of five Bangladeshi expatriate workers who were killed in a road accident in Qatar have arrived in Bangladesh.
The remains were flown back to the Middle Eastern nation to their home country for burial.
The arrival of the bodies at the airport was met with grieving family members and relatives who came to receive them.
The victims were migrant workers who had gone to Qatar to earn a living for their families back home.
caption:
Five Bangladeshi workers killed in a road crash in Qatar have finally returned home.

The bodies of five Bangladeshi expatriate workers who were killed in a road accident in Qatar have arrived in Bangladesh.

The remains were flown back to the Middle Eastern nation to their home country for burial.

The arrival of the bodies at the airport was met with grieving family members and relatives who came to receive them.

The victims were migrant workers who had gone to Qatar to earn a living for their families back home.

headline_marked: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: [[Equipment worth 27cr bought for 214cr]]
headline: Rooppur Nuclear Plant: Equipment worth 27cr bought for 214cr
summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) found massive irregularities in the procurement of electrical equipment for the plant's residential area.
details: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has uncovered massive irregularities in the procurement of electrical equipment and generators for 'Green City', the residential area of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant.
According to the audit, equipment with a government-set price of approximately 27 crore BDT was purchased for 213.88 crore BDT, resulting in an overpayment of about 186.89 crore BDT.

The audit report states that the Public Works Department (PWD) caused significant financial loss to the government by purchasing equipment at prices abnormally higher than official estimates and government rates.
Irregularities were found across nearly every stage of the process, including tender preparation, tender evaluation, work orders, bill approval, and payment.
In one specific building, high-voltage control equipment worth 10.32 lakh BDT was billed at 4.5 crore BDT, while a distribution transformer worth 40.4 lakh BDT was billed at 4.4 crore BDT.
Three contractors—Majid Sons Construction Ltd, Sajin Enterprise, and an MSCL-GKBP joint venture—were paid a total of 213.89 crore BDT for equipment that should have cost 26.99 crore BDT.
The CAG recommended administrative action against those involved and the recovery of the misappropriated funds to the government treasury.
The audit also noted that the tender evaluation committee failed to follow government procurement rules, which require explanations for abnormally high prices proposed by bidders.
caption:
27 crore BDT worth of equipment was billed at 214 crore BDT. A massive procurement scandal has surfaced at the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant.

The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has uncovered massive irregularities in the procurement of electrical equipment and generators for 'Green City', the residential area of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant.

According to the audit, equipment with a government-set price of approximately 27 crore BDT was purchased for 213.88 crore BDT, resulting in an overpayment of about 186.89 crore BDT.

The audit report states that the Public Works Department (PWD) caused significant financial loss to the government by purchasing equipment at prices abnormally higher than official estimates and government rates.

Irregularities were found across nearly every stage of the process, including tender preparation, tender evaluation, work orders, bill approval, and payment.

In one specific building, high-voltage control equipment worth 10.32 lakh BDT was billed at 4.5 crore BDT, while a distribution transformer worth 40.4 lakh BDT was billed at 4.4 crore BDT.

Three contractors—Majid Sons Construction Ltd, Sajin Enterprise, and an MSCL-GKBP joint venture—were paid a total of 213.89 crore BDT for equipment that should have cost 26.99 crore BDT.

The CAG recommended administrative action against those involved and the recovery of the misappropriated funds to the government treasury.

The audit also noted that the tender evaluation committee failed to follow government procurement rules, which require explanations for abnormally high prices proposed by bidders.
